title: x86-64 GDT (Global Descriptor Table) entry
summary: An x86-64 GDT entry is 8 bytes (64 bits) for a code/data segment, or 16 bytes for a system segment (TSS, LDT, gate). Code/data segment: base (32 bits, split), limit (20 bits, split), access byte (8 bits: present, DPL, S, type), flags (4 bits: granularity, default size, long mode, available). In long mode (64-bit), base and limit are mostly ignored (flat model).

structure.meaning: Low 16 bits of the segment limit.
Low 16 bits of the base address.
Bit 7 = Present, bits 5-6 = DPL, bit 4 = S (1=code/data, 0=system), bits 0-3 = Type (code: execute/read, data: read/write, etc.).
Bits 0-3 = Limit bits 16-19, bit 4 = Available, bit 5 = Long mode (L), bit 6 = Default size (D/B), bit 7 = Granularity (G, 0=byte, 1=4KB).

ext.example_decoded: x86-64 GDT entry: all zeros (null descriptor)
notes: In 64-bit long mode, segmentation is mostly flat (base=0, limit=2^64-1).
GDT must have at least 3 entries: null, code segment, data segment.
TSS (Task State Segment) descriptor is 16 bytes (two 8-byte entries).
LDT (Local Descriptor Table) is rarely used in modern OSes.
GDT is loaded via LGDT instruction (points to GDTR).
